Task complete. Here's what happened.

## Result

`ADS-DUMMY-001-R1` is **COMPLETED**. I created `ads_dummy.txt` at the repository root with the exact required content, the requested validation command passed with exit code 0, and I committed the file to the task branch as `6b1267d`. No merge, no push, no simulation, no installs.

## What I did

**Artifact.** `ads_dummy.txt` contains `round 1 complete` followed by a single LF (17 bytes, no BOM). I verified the bytes with `od -c` rather than trusting the write, and confirmed the committed Git blob (`git cat-file -p HEAD:ads_dummy.txt`) has identical LF bytes.

**Validation.** The requested command is PASS with exit code 0, run both before and after the commit:

```
python -c "from pathlib import Path; assert Path('ads_dummy.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8') == 'round 1 complete\n'"
```

I also added three read-only checks beyond the request: the byte dump above, the blob byte dump, and `git show | cat -A`, which shows a single added line `+round 1 complete$` as `new file mode 100644`.

**Git state.** Base `f36d7d4`, head `6b1267d`, branch `agent-task/ADS-DUMMY-001`, working tree clean afterward. The commit contains only `ads_dummy.txt` — `.agent_runtime/` is gitignored, so the report is not part of it.

**Scope.** Only the two allowed paths were written. No solver, boundary, initial-condition, convergence, test, data, results, or scientific-documentation file was touched, and no solver code path was executed — so there is no scientific or modeling impact, and no synchronization with the separate `LBM/source_code/taichi_LBM3D/2phase/` tree is needed.

## Two things worth your attention

**I committed, but did not push.** The task's evidence request named a *candidate commit*, and its git policy permits commit and push to the task branch without requiring the push. Since the branch has no upstream, pushing would create a new `agent-task/ADS-DUMMY-001` branch on `origin`. I made the commit locally and left the push to the controller. If you wanted the push done as part of this round, that is a one-command follow-up.

**An environment detail that will matter in Round 2.** `core.autocrlf=true` is set in this worktree, so a fresh checkout on this machine may materialize the file with CRLF even though the committed blob is LF. The validation still passes in that case, because `Path.read_text()` applies universal newline translation — I confirmed this without writing any file, by reading a `\r\n` byte stream through `TextIOWrapper` and checking it equals `'round 1 complete\n'`. Worth knowing because `git grep` also shows `.agent/examples/dummy/ROUND_2_TASK.md` expects this file to grow to two lines; the same newline behavior will apply there.

The report is at `.agent_runtime/execution_report.md`. **Suggested next action:** review commit `6b1267d` against the Round 1 acceptance criteria and decide whether to authorize Round 2.
